project_members_core.name: project_members_core
project_members_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  project,
  pic_number,
  rcn,
  member_name,
  activity_type,
  country,
  street,
  city,
  postal_code,
  ec_contribution,
  institution_id,
  member_role,
  geocode_regions_3,
  member_short_name,
  department_name,
  vat_number,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  region_code,
  region_name
FROM
  project_members

params.description: Provides one-row-per-project-member details (financial and address attributes) for project participants, answering who the member is, their role, contribution and geolocation within a project.
params.when_to_use: List project members and their EC contribution amounts for a given project or set of projects (by project, rcn, or pic_number). | Filter or group members by country, region_code/region_name, geocode_regions_3, member_role, activity_type or institution_id. | Join member-level attributes to project-level results when composing aggregations (after ensuring correct cardinality handling). | Enrich analytics with member contact/address details (street, city, postal_code, vat_number) or geolocation (latitude, longitude).
params.output_schema: unics_id: unique identifier of the project member row — derived directly from project_members.unics_id | project: project identifier (string) — derived directly from project_members.project | pic_number: PIC (participant identification code) of the member — derived directly from project_members.pic_number | rcn: the project's RCN (research council number) — derived directly from project_members.rcn | member_name: full name of the member organization/person — derived directly from project_members.member_name | activity_type: activity category of the member within the project — derived directly from project_members.activity_type | country: member country (ISO/name as stored) — derived directly from project_members.country | street: street address of the member — derived directly from project_members.street | city: city of the member — derived directly from project_members.city | postal_code: postal / ZIP code of the member — derived directly from project_members.postal_code | ec_contribution: monetary contribution value from the EC for this member (numeric) — derived directly from project_members.ec_contribution | institution_id: internal institution identifier (if present) — derived directly from project_members.institution_id | member_role: role of the member in the project (e.g., coordinator, participant) — derived directly from project_members.member_role | geocode_regions_3: 3-level geocode region classification for the member — derived directly from project_members.geocode_regions_3 | member_short_name: abbreviated name for the member — derived directly from project_members.member_short_name | department_name: department within the member institution — derived directly from project_members.department_name | vat_number: VAT/VAT-like tax identifier for the member — derived directly from project_members.vat_number | latitude: latitude coordinate for the member location (numeric) — derived directly from project_members.latitude | longitude: longitude coordinate for the member location (numeric) — derived directly from project_members.longitude | region_code: administrative region code for the member (e.g., NUTS) — derived directly from project_members.region_code | region_name: administrative region name for the member — derived directly from project_members.region_name
params.grounded_columns: project_members.unics_id | project_members.project | project_members.pic_number | project_members.rcn | project_members.member_name | project_members.activity_type | project_members.country | project_members.street | project_members.city | project_members.postal_code | project_members.ec_contribution | project_members.institution_id | project_members.member_role | project_members.geocode_regions_3 | project_members.member_short_name | project_members.department_name | project_members.vat_number | project_members.latitude | project_members.longitude | project_members.region_code | project_members.region_name
params.metric: ec_contribution = project_members.ec_contribution  -- atomic monetary measure at the unics_id (member) grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a project dimension (one-row-per-project) on project_members.project = project_dim.project_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-unics_id (member). Joining to a one-row-per-project table will not duplicate member rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to an institution lookup (one-row-per-institution) on project_members.institution_id = institution.institution_id — safe because institution is expected to be one-to-one with institution_id and will not duplicate this view's rows. | do NOT join directly to tables or views that are one-to-many from unics_id (for example: a timesheet, invoice, or any transaction table keyed to unics_id) without re-aggregation. Such joins would multiply ec_contribution and other member-level attributes. If you need metrics from a one-to-many table, first aggregate that table to the unics_id grain (e.g., SUM(amount) GROUP BY unics_id) and then join to project_members on unics_id. | do NOT join to project_members-like sibling member lists (another member-level table) on project without a pre-aggregation step, because joining two member-level lists by project will produce a cross-product of members and inflate counts/sums. To combine different member lists, aggregate each to the desired grain (e.g., per-project or per-unics_id) before joining. | when aggregating up from this view to project-level metrics (e.g., total EC contribution per project), use GROUP BY project and aggregate ec_contribution (SUM) — this is correct because ec_contribution is recorded at the unics_id (member) grain. | example safe composition pattern: (SELECT project, SUM(ec_contribution) AS project_ec FROM project_members_core GROUP BY project) JOIN project_dim USING(project) — safe because the SUM collapses member rows to project-level before joining.

project_members_core.description: Canonical projection of project_members preserving identifiers and key participant attributes (institution linkage, ec_contribution, geocode and region). Useful for participant-level analyses and joins to institutions or projects. | Use for: List or count of participants per project; Aggregate EC contributions by institution or country; Mapping participants to regions or geocodes

projects_time_dimensions.name: projects_time_dimensions
projects_time_dimensions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date,
  -- lift literals: none required; use project's existing year/month/quarter logic
  -- prefer existing start_year if present, otherwise extract year from start_date
  COALESCE(p.start_year,
           CASE WHEN p.start_date IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.start_date)::int END
          ) AS start_year,
  -- start_month derived from start_date (1-12) or NULL
  CASE WHEN p.start_date IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM p.start_date)::int END AS start_month,
  -- start_quarter derived from start_date (1-4) or NULL
  CASE WHEN p.start_date IS NOT NULL THEN ((EXTRACT(MONTH FROM p.start_date)::int - 1) / 3 + 1) END AS start_quarter
FROM projects_rowlevel p
projects_time_dimensions.description: Normalized time-related attributes for projects to make date-based filters and groupings easy (year, month, quarter).

project_financials_by_project.name: project_financials_by_project
project_financials_by_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  -- prefer normalized/aggregated cost if available, else fall back to raw projects.total_cost
  COALESCE(pc.total_cost, p.total_cost) AS total_cost,
  -- prefer aggregated/ec-determined max contribution if available, else use projects.ec_max_contribution
  COALESCE(pc.ec_max_contribution, p.ec_max_contribution) AS ec_max_contribution
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN project_costs_by_id pc
  ON pc.unics_id = p.unics_id
project_financials_by_project.description: Per-project financial measures derived/normalized from projects table to support ranking and aggregation (keeps one row per project with raw measures ready for higher-level aggregations).

project_members_row_level.name: project_members_row_level
project_members_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the member's unique id (grain)
  pm.unics_id AS unics_id,

  -- project linkage (may be NULL in source; coalesce to 0 to avoid NULLs in foreign key)
  COALESCE(pm.project, 0) AS project,

  -- member name: prefer member_name, fall back to member_short_name, else blank
  COALESCE(NULLIF(pm.member_name, ''), NULLIF(pm.member_short_name, ''), '') AS member_name,

  -- member role: keep as-is, coalesce to 'unknown' when NULL
  COALESCE(NULLIF(pm.member_role, ''), 'unknown') AS member_role,

  -- institution linkage: keep institution_id, coalesce to 0 when NULL
  COALESCE(pm.institution_id, 0) AS institution_id,

  -- ec_contribution: keep numeric value, coalesce NULL to 0.0
  COALESCE(pm.ec_contribution, 0.0) AS ec_contribution,

  -- country: keep country text, coalesce to empty string when NULL
  COALESCE(NULLIF(pm.country, ''), '') AS country,

  -- region_code: carry through region_code, coalesce to empty string
  COALESCE(NULLIF(pm.region_code, ''), '') AS region_code,

  -- latitude / longitude: keep numeric, leave NULLs as NULL (but could coalesce to 0.0 if desired)
  pm.latitude AS latitude,
  pm.longitude AS longitude
FROM project_members_core pm
project_members_row_level.description: One row per project member with member identity, role, and link to project and institution; cleans NULLs for member_name and core foreign keys.

FROM project_members_core pm
WHERE pm.project IS NOT NULL
project_members_raw.description: Row-level project member records; filters out rows with NULL project to produce a reusable cohort of members assigned to projects.

project_member_counts_by_project.name: project_member_counts_by_project
project_member_counts_by_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  COUNT(*) AS member_row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pm.unics_id) AS distinct_member_count
FROM
  project_members_core pm
GROUP BY
  pm.project
-- Lift filter literals out of the view (apply WHERE in queries selecting from this view)
project_member_counts_by_project.description: Aggregated counts of members per project: total rows and distinct member IDs. One row per project allowing filters by minimum member counts.

projects_row_level_32.name: projects_row_level_32
projects_row_level_32.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.ec_fund_scheme AS ec_fund_scheme,
  p.title        AS title,
  p.start_date   AS start_date,
  p.end_date     AS end_date,
  p.framework_program AS framework_program
FROM projects p

semantic_filters.ec_fund_scheme: IS NOT NULL (optional filter applied later)

projects_row_level_32.description: One row per project exposing funding scheme and other project attributes for filtering, grouping and joins.

funding_schemes_canonical.name: funding_schemes_canonical
funding_schemes_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  fs.code AS code,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(trim(fs.title), ''), fs.code) AS title
FROM funding_schemes fs
funding_schemes_canonical.description: Canonical list of funding schemes with code and normalized title; suitable for joining to projects.ec_fund_scheme.

projects_by_funding_scheme_agg.name: projects_by_funding_scheme_agg
projects_by_funding_scheme_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  pr.ec_fund_scheme AS ec_fund_scheme,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pr.unics_id) AS project_count
FROM
  projects_rowlevel pr
GROUP BY
  pr.ec_fund_scheme

semantic_filters.ec_fund_scheme: IS NOT NULL (only include projects with a non-null ec_fund_scheme)

projects_by_funding_scheme_agg.description: Aggregated counts of projects per funding scheme code (one row per funding scheme code) for ranking or reporting.

project_titles_for_filters.name: project_titles_for_filters
project_titles_for_filters.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year
FROM projects_rowlevel p
project_titles_for_filters.description: Lightweight view joining project identifiers to title and key temporal fields to be used when answering title-selection queries after applying temporal or other filters.

project_principal_investigator_and_insti.name: project_principal_investigator_and_institution
project_principal_investigator_and_insti.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.principal_investigator,
  p.pi_full_name,
  pm.institution_id
FROM
  project_with_principal_investigator p
LEFT JOIN
  project_members_core pm
ON
  p.unics_id = pm.project
  AND pm.member_role = 'principal_investigator'
project_principal_investigator_and_insti.description: Denormalized mapping of a project to its principal investigator (person) and the PI's institution id (if available). Useful for questions that join project-level metrics to people or institutions.

topics_core.name: topics_core
topics_core.description: Canonical projection of the topics table exposing topic identifiers and title for downstream filtering and joins. Performs minimal cleaning (preserve NULLs) and exposes stable key.

topics_text_normalized.name: topics_text_normalized
topics_text_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  code,
  -- canonicalized title: trim whitespace and collapse internal whitespace to single space
  regexp_replace(trim(title), '\s+', ' ', 'g') AS title,
  lower(regexp_replace(trim(title), '\s+', ' ', 'g')) AS lowercase_title
FROM topics
topics_text_normalized.description: Normalized projection of the topics table that exposes topic id and canonicalized title and a lowercase_title column to support case-insensitive text matching.

topics_cohort.name: topics_cohort
topics_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.code,
  t.rcn,
  t.title
FROM topics t
topics_cohort.description: Row-level selectable cohort of topics with basic metadata; use this as the base for any topic-level filtering (e.g., text search, joins to project_topic).

projects_with_pi.name: projects_with_pi
projects_with_pi.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS pi_full_name,
  p.title,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN people pe
  ON p.principal_investigator = pe.unics_id
projects_with_pi.description: Denormalized join of projects to people (principal investigator) exposing project rows with PI identity and name for easy cohort selection by person name.

people_core.name: people_core
people_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  full_name
FROM
  people
WHERE
  unics_id IS NOT NULL
people_core.description: Normalized/cleaned projection of the people table exposing the person id and canonical full name. Filters out rows with NULL id (ensures valid primary key) but does not drop NULL full_name so it can be used for cleaning workflows.

countries_lookup.name: countries_lookup
countries_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.unics_id,
  c.country_name,
  c.country_code2,
  c.country_code3,
  c.geocode_country_code
FROM
  countries c
countries_lookup.description: Canonical country lookup table exposing country id and canonical country_name and common codes for joining from other tables.
validated_on: What is the country code 2 and country code 3 for Andorra?

institutions_with_country_denorm.name: institutions_with_country_denorm
institutions_with_country_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id,
  i.institutions_name,
  c.country_name,
  i.country_id,
  i.geocode_regions_3,
  c.country_code2,
  c.country_code3
FROM institutions i
LEFT JOIN countries c
  ON i.country_id = c.unics_id
institutions_with_country_denorm.description: One row per institution, with the matched country name when available by joining institutions.country_id to countries.unics_id. Keeps institution identifiers and core location fields for downstream filters or aggregations.

institutions_canonical_names.name: institutions_canonical_names
institutions_canonical_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id,
  -- canonical institutions_name: prefer cleaned short_name if it's a clear real name, else institutions_name;
  -- lift any string literals out of view: none needed here
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(trim(i.institutions_name), ''),
    NULLIF(trim(i.short_name), ''),
    NULLIF(trim(i.acronym), '')
  ) AS institutions_name,
  NULLIF(trim(i.short_name), '') AS short_name,
  NULLIF(trim(i.acronym), '') AS acronym,
  NULLIF(trim(i.website), '') AS website
FROM institutions i
institutions_canonical_names.description: Normalized/cleaned projection of institutions exposing canonical name and key identifiers. Useful when queries need a stable institution name field and keys for joins; does not assume any specific filtering.

countries_core.name: countries_core
countries_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  country_name,
  country_code2,
  country_code3,
  geocode_country_code
FROM countries
countries_core.description: Core country reference table projection exposing primary country identifiers and standard codes for joining and display.

funding_schemes_core.name: funding_schemes_core
funding_schemes_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  fs.code AS code,
  fs.title AS title
FROM funding_schemes fs
funding_schemes_core.description: One-row-per-funding-scheme with its identifying code and human title; minimal cleaning applied.

funding_schemes_normalized_titles.name: funding_schemes_normalized_titles
funding_schemes_normalized_titles.body_sql:
SELECT
  fs.code,
  fs.title,
  -- Lifted literals: none needed beyond functions
  -- Normalize by: lowercasing, trimming, collapsing internal whitespace to single space
  -- Keep NULL title as NULL for title_normalized
  CASE
    WHEN fs.title IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE regexp_replace(trim(lower(fs.title)), '\s+', ' ', 'g')
  END AS title_normalized
FROM funding_schemes fs
funding_schemes_normalized_titles.description: Normalized titles for funding schemes to support case-insensitive and whitespace-robust matching; preserves the funding_schemes.code as the key.

projects_with_funding_scheme.name: projects_with_funding_scheme
projects_with_funding_scheme.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  fs.title AS funding_scheme_title
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN funding_schemes fs
  ON p.ec_fund_scheme = fs.code
projects_with_funding_scheme.description: Projects joined to their funding scheme code and title; one row per projects.unics_id. Useful for questions that filter projects by funding scheme or need to report project-level data alongside the scheme.

programmes_core.name: programmes_core
programmes_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.code,
  p.rcn,
  p.title,
  p.short_name,
  p.parent
FROM
  programmes p
programmes_core.description: Canonical programme rows with core identifying and descriptive columns normalized for queries. Keeps one row per programme and exposes keys and common text fields used for filtering and display.

programmes_by_short_name_cohort.name: programmes_by_short_name_cohort
programmes_by_short_name_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  code,
  short_name,
  title
FROM programmes
ORDER BY code
programmes_by_short_name_cohort.description: Selectable cohort of programmes exposing program key and short_name for quick lookup/filtering by short_name or patterns. One row per programme.

project_members_with_project.name: project_members_with_project
project_members_with_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  pm.project AS project,
  p.unics_id AS projects_unics_id,
  p.acronym AS projects_acronym
FROM
  project_members_core pm
LEFT JOIN
  projects_row_level p
ON
  pm.project = p.unics_id
project_members_with_project.description: Denormalized join of project_members to projects to produce one row per project member with the linked project acronym and project identifiers. Useful for queries that select members by project attributes (e.g., project acronym).
